title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Eligibility Matrix by Debt Type, Stage, Balance and Channel
content:
Whether a tier of **Hardship and Protective Holds** can be granted on a placed account depends on the account's debt type, its placement stage and its balance due, and on the channel through which the request arrives. Two further tier settings appear in this matrix: the disaster declaration look-back and whether one approved request covers all of the consumer's eligible accounts.

## Entry condition of each tier

| Tier | Entry condition |
|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | Documentation by self-attestation |
| Documented Hardship Hold | Documented income loss |
| Disaster Relief Hold | Primary residence in a declared disaster area |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | A medical debt, and a financial assistance application submitted |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | A qualifying condition of serious illness, disability or long-term unemployment |
| Military Service Hold | The consumer or the consumer's spouse on active duty |

## Debt types each tier may hold

| Tier | Eligible debt types |
|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | Medical, bank card, utility, telecom, auto deficiency, private student loan, retail installment |
| Documented Hardship Hold | Medical, bank card, utility, telecom, auto deficiency, private student loan, retail installment |
| Disaster Relief Hold | Medical, bank card, utility, telecom, auto deficiency, private student loan, retail installment |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | Medical only |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | Medical, bank card, utility, telecom, auto deficiency, private student loan, retail installment |
| Military Service Hold | Medical, bank card, utility, telecom, auto deficiency, private student loan, retail installment |

## Placement stages each tier may hold

| Tier | Early-Out | Primary | Secondary | Tertiary | Warehouse | Legal Review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Documented Hardship Hold | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Disaster Relief Hold | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Military Service Hold | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

(The stage columns are Early-Out Placement, Primary Placement, Secondary Placement, Tertiary Placement, Warehouse Placement and Legal Review Placement.)

## Balance, channels and tier-wide settings

| Tier | Smallest balance due granted (USD) | Request channels | Disaster declaration look-back (calendar days) | One request covers all eligible accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | 25.00 | Phone, online portal, email | 0 | No |
| Documented Hardship Hold | 100.00 | Phone, online portal, email, mail | 0 | No |
| Disaster Relief Hold | 0.00 (any balance) | Phone, online portal, email, mail | 120 | Yes |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | 0.00 (any balance) | Phone, online portal, email, mail, fax | 0 | No |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | 250.00 | Online portal, email, mail, fax | 0 | No |
| Military Service Hold | 0.00 (any balance) | Phone, online portal, email, mail, fax | 0 | Yes |

- **Smallest balance due granted** — the smallest balance due on which the tier is granted; 0.00 means any balance.
- **Disaster declaration look-back** — the calendar days after the disaster declaration date within which the hold must be requested; 0 where the tier is not a disaster tier.
- **One request covers all eligible accounts** — whether one approved request places a hold on every open eligible account of the consumer.

## Points of reading

- The Long-Term Hardship Hold cannot be requested by phone; its request channels are the online portal, email, mail and fax.
- A balance due exactly equal to the tier's figure meets it: a 30-Day Hardship Pause can be granted on a balance due of 25.00, but not on 24.99.
- The Financial Assistance Review Hold is confined to medical debts at the Early-Out, Primary, Secondary and Tertiary stages.
